skills.name: Simplify surds, rationalise denominators and bound an irrational number

note.text:
A surd is a root that is not a whole number, such as √2 or 3√5. Leave it exact unless a decimal is asked for.
• Simplify: take out the largest square factor. √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2.
• Like surds add like terms: 3√2 + 5√2 = 8√2. √8 + √18 = 2√2 + 3√2 = 5√2.
• √a × √b = √(ab); √a × √a = a.
• Rationalise a denominator: 6/√3 = 6√3/3 = 2√3. For 1/(√5 − 2) multiply top and bottom by √5 + 2: (√5 + 2)/(5 − 4) = √5 + 2.
• Bounds: 36 < 40 < 49, so 6 < √40 < 7.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to simplify and add surds, rationalise denominators (including √a − b) and place a root between two whole numbers.
Builds on: Form Three square roots and Lesson {3} (the difference of two squares).
Leads to: exact answers in trigonometry, the quadratic formula and Form Five surd equations.

sections.heading: Simplifying and adding
sections.text:
√{72} is not a whole number, but it can be simplified. Look for the largest square factor: {72} = {36} × {2}.
√{72} = √{36} × √{2} = {surd(72)}.
Surds with the same root are like terms: {surd(8)} + {surd(18)} = {surd(2, 2)} + {surd(2, 3)} = {surd(2, 5)}.
But √{2} + √{3} cannot be combined, and √{9} + √{16} = {7}, not √{25}.
Bounds: {36} < {40} < {49}, so {6} < √{40} < {7}.

sections.heading: Rationalising
sections.text:
A root in the denominator is usually removed.
• {6}/√{3}: multiply top and bottom by √{3}: {6}√{3}/{3} = {surd(3, 2)}.
• {1}/(√{5} − {2}): multiply by the conjugate √{5} + {2}. The bottom becomes {5} − {4} = {1} (a difference of two squares), so the answer is √{5} + {2}.
Multiplying top and bottom by the same thing does not change the value, only its form.

key_words.meaning: an exact root that is not a whole number, such as √{2}
rewrite with no root in the denominator
the same two terms with the middle sign changed: √{5} + {2} for √{5} − {2}

questions.prompt: √{n} lies between two consecutive whole numbers. What is the smaller one?

misconceptions.explain: √{n} is not half of {n}: find the squares on each side of {n}.
That is the larger one.
